rows.subtype: Turning away as boundary or snub [Interpreting]
rows.description: A teenager reads a peer turning away as a snub, but it may mean the person is distracted or needs space. Not taking it personally, and asking later, keeps friendships steadier.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A teenager rolls the shoulders to release tension before a match or exam, or holds them tense when anxious. Noticing and releasing them is a useful calming tool.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A teenager shrugs in response to a parent's question, which may mean I do not care, I do not know how to say it or I am upset. Patient open questions often unlock a real answer.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.subtype: Folded arms as boundary or comfort [Mismatch]
rows.description: A teenager folds the arms to signal a boundary, to feel cold or to feel secure. Interpreting it as closed-off without checking can be unfair.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A teenager opens the arms for a friend who is upset, offering comfort, and learns to ask first if a hug is welcome. Consent applies to every hug, and a refusal is respected.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.subtype: Clapping and snapping in peer groups [Expressing]
rows.description: A teenager claps or snaps as approval among friends, or slowly claps sarcastically. Tone and speed show whether it is praise or mockery.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A teenager reads open palms as honesty or welcome, but it is only one cue and is not proof someone is truthful.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A teenager uses air quotes to signal irony or doubt and a mock salute for humour or respect. The tone decides if it is friendly teasing or a put-down.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: amusement, admiration, doubt

rows.description: A teenager recognises thumbs-down and rude gestures, including the raised middle finger, as insults or strong disapproval, and learns to step back, stay calm and tell an adult if it comes from bullying. Using them hurts others and can bring consequences.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A teenager in an online class uses the raise-hand button, a chat emoji or a mute icon to take turns without speaking over others. The tool replaces the physical gesture, but silence in a video call is ambiguous and may mean shyness, lag or disengagement.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26
